_engine_finding: *** On a SHARED wall each room's wall MASS lands inside its NEIGHBOUR. *** house.js extrudes walls OUTWARD from the footprint line (WALL_THICKNESS 0.35, `geo.translate(0,0,-t)`), so the Movie Room's north wall body occupies world z 11.05-11.40 (inside the Arcade) and the Arcade Room's south wall body occupies world z 11.40-11.75 -- i.e. Movie-local z 0 to 0.35. Everything round 1 put on the north wall at depth < 0.35 (the screen at 0.19, the in-wall speakers at 0.10, the chair rail at 0.085, the wainscot at 0.042, the baseboard at 0.075) was BURIED and invisible from inside the room, and what you actually saw was the Arcade's wall face. That is the true cause of round 1's `_gaps` entry 'the north wall is CLIPPED at 238 with no chair-rail step' -- it was never tone-curve saturation. Every north-wall element is now authored at depth >= NF = 0.36 and the north wall meters 161.9 with a proper 26-point rail step.

_camera.why: cutaway.js fades the two walls nearest the camera. This room's content is on the NORTH wall (TV, console, subs, door) and the WEST wall (art, window, sectional) -- doll_se culls SOUTH and EAST and is the only quadrant that leaves both standing. It also matches the level-0 whole-floor pose. The new stair partition is >1 ft from any room wall so cutaway leaves it alone, which is right: it is a real interior wall, not a skin.

_metered._how: Render values from --day --no-cutaway shots at NATIVE resolution, 1100x850 look_n/s/e/w from the room centre (clean wall boxes only, verified against a _boxes overlay). Photo values from 'Movie Room v3 4.jpg' at its native 1200x1600 -- the ONLY v3 shot big enough to meter; v3 2/3/5 are 450x600 and their sd is scale-inflated. Both sd AND mean|adjacent-pixel delta| are reported, per ROOM-BRIEF 'sd is SCALE-BLIND'. Shots: scratchpad/shots/v3_movie/.

_how_the_wall_skins_were_solved: Two-point probe, per wall and per band, exactly as ROOM-BRIEF prescribes: build once at one albedo, meter a clean box on that wall in its own look_* render, rebuild at a second albedo, meter again, fit render = a + b*albedo_sRGB, invert for the target (upper 158, wainscot 136), rebuild, verify. Three iterations were needed on the north wall because its response is strongly non-linear (there is a large additive term: even a near-black skin renders ~97 up there). Final albedos: upper N #6a6c6f W #a4a6a9 E #d3d5d8 S #fbfdff; wainscot N #56585b W #8f9194 E #babcbf S #dadce0. Note how far apart those are -- the same paint value renders 220 on the north wall and 139 on the south -- which is precisely why one wall_color could never work. NONE of them is emissive; each is a full-height, corner-to-corner plane at roughness 0.95 (matching the room wall) carrying a tiled grain PNG plus smooth per-vertex colour jitter, so no skin ships at sd 0.00.
_gaps: FABRIC FINE-SCALE GRADIENT is still short of the photo. Upholstery now meters |d1| 1.85-3.40 against the photo's 3.11-10.96 (round 1's fabrics were 0.07, effectively plastic). The lift came from giving every upholstery part a planar UV projection so the woven tile actually samples, plus per-vertex colour. The residue is a tessellation limit: puff/slab carry too few vertices for the vertex-colour term to vary at 1-2 inch scale, and the tile is minified at typical viewing distance. Closing it fully needs UV-generating primitives in roomkit.glb, not more geometry (that is the Kitchen's 5.88 MB mistake).

The CEILING meters sd 0.72 against the photo's 2.39-2.95. Its tile is there but a downward plane at 8 ft is minified almost to a flat colour. Left alone rather than cranking the tile contrast, which would show as visible mosaic from the doll pose.

The room's SE quadrant (local x 15.2-20.4, z 16.3-23.5, ~24 sq ft) is bare plank. That is what the plan shows -- it is the landing you step into off the stair -- but a critic may read it as unfurnished floor.

The v3 photos disagree with each other about where the black cabinet / ring fan cluster sits. Photo 4 (primary, 1200x1600) puts it on the wall LEFT of the SW corner, which is the south wall's east end, and that is what is built. Photo 2 (450x600) reads it as nearer the west wall. The plan shows no blob for it either way. If the owner says otherwise, move 'Movie Corner Props' -- nothing else depends on it.

The SOUTH window's x position (local 2.40-6.00) is the weakest number in the build: it comes from a camera solve on photo 4's ultrawide frame (SW corner at frame x 740 of 1200), good to maybe +-1.5 ft. Its existence is certain (photo 2 and photo 4 both show it); its offset is not.

Not modelled: the white electrical panel and thermostat, the console's exact hardware, the wall outlet plates, and the small return register. The five-panel print is a procedurally generated dark-massed-figures image, not the owner's actual artwork.

_contact_shadows: Rebuilt. kit.contact_shadow runs its 12 annuli from s=1.0 down to s=0.10, so with rx near the footprint almost all the darkness lands UNDER the piece: measured 9% darkening at the contact edge against ROOM-BRIEF's 34% target. mv2.py's own `cshadow()` takes the piece's HALF-EXTENTS and runs the ramp from 0.55x them out to (h + 0.8 ft) with exponent 1.15, so about half the layers overlap at the footprint edge. Measured in the top-down render: 30% darkening at the contact edge, easing to zero over ~20 px, under the sectional, the ottoman and both chairs. Heights: floor plane 0.042, rug 0.046-0.098, shadows on bare plank 0.058, shadows on the rug 0.104 -- all well clear of the slab's polygonOffset.
